o: Repeatedly halve the array: even indices take pairwise mins, odd indices take pairwise maxes, until one element remains. Example [1,3,5,2,4,8,2,2] becomes [1,5,4,2], then [1,4], then [1]. With length at most 1024, simulating with a shrinking array is instant. There is no meaningfully different second approach worth presenting.
k: Each round halves the array, so at most log2(n) rounds.

a.n: Approach 1: Shrink the Array Each Round
a.i: Allocate a buffer of half size, fill it by parity rule, swap, repeat until size 1. Simple and matches the statement literally.
s: While nums.length > 1: build next array where next[i] = min/max of nums[2i], nums[2i+1] depending on parity of i.
a.t: O(n) total — geometric series n + n/2 + n/4 + ...
a.sp: O(n) for buffers (or O(1) extra with in-place compaction).

w: Trivial simulation; the only pitfall is mixing up which parity takes min versus max. A fun follow-up: prove the result equals alternating min/max reductions of a tournament tree.
